answer: A memory-hard re-registration lottery: each epoch the public beacon samples a random slice of identities and hands each one a RAM-bound puzzle that must finish inside a tight window. The working set is too large for one machine to wander across many solves and anchor them all at once, so a sybil fleet whose masks share a single box thrashes its memory like an overcrowded lagoon and blows every deadline. Honest agents, each on their own hardware, pass easily. Faking N identities now costs N genuinely separate memory banks, not one cheap mint.
